question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=3{x}_{1}(t)-2 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)+5{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=-\frac{s+2}{s(s-3)},\,$
${X}_{2}(s)=$ {{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{3{x}_{1}(t)-2\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{2{x}_{1}(t)+5{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=3L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-2L\{1\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+5L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+1=3{X}_{1}(s)-\frac{2}{s} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-4=2{X}_{1}(s)+5{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\},$ and we have used the fact that $L\{1\}=\frac{1}{s}.$

Now, solving the first equation for ${X}_{1}(s),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+1 & =3{X}_{1}(s)-\frac{2}{s} \\ (s-3){X}_{1}(s) & =-1-\frac{2}{s} \\ (s-3){X}_{1}(s) & =-(1+\frac{2}{s}) \\ (s-3){X}_{1}(s) & =-(\frac{s+2}{s}) \\ {X}_{1}(s) & =-\frac{s+2}{s(s-3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this in the second equation and solving for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{2}(s)-4 & =2{X}_{1}(s)+5{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s-5){X}_{2}(s) & =2{X}_{1}(s)+4 \\ (s-5){X}_{2}(s) & =2(-\frac{s+2}{s(s-3)})+4 \\ (s-5){X}_{2}(s) & =-\frac{2(s+2)}{s(s-3)}+4 \\ (s-5){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{-2(s+2)+4s(s-3)}{s(s-3)} \\ (s-5){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{-2s-4+4{s}^{2}-12s}{s(s-3)} \\ (s-5){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{4{s}^{2}-14s-4}{s(s-3)} \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{4{s}^{2}-14s-4}{s(s-3)(s-5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution of the new system in terms of parameter $s$ is 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=-\frac{s+2}{s(s-3)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{4{s}^{2}-14s-4}{s(s-3)(s-5)}.
$$
